item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work introduces two orthogonal descriptors—effective hydroxyl density and minimum electrostatic potential—to rationally screen polyol hydrogen-bond donors for hydrated eutectic electrolytes. Erythritol optimally balances interfacial adsorption and desolvation, enabling 6740 h symmetric cycling and 11,400 full-cell cycles. It shifts electrolyte design from empirical trial to quantitative molecular criteria.

💡 The novelty lies in using hydroxyethyl cellulose to "stitch" pores in acid/alkali-purified biomass hard carbon, reconstructing the disrupted framework and reducing irreversible capacity loss. 💡 This work bypasses lithium salt solubility limits by immobilizing insoluble Li₂SO₄ on an aramid-scaffolded separator, creating a LiF-rich SEI via regulated solvation. Scalable at 0.163 USD m⁻², it unlocks vast high-lattice-energy salts for next-generation batteries.

item.title: Tailored ZnO/Cellulose Separator Reconfigures Solvation Chemistry for Durable Magnesium Metal Batteries
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work introduces a ZnO/cellulose composite separator that anchors solvent molecules via bidirectional charge transfer, reconfiguring Mg²⁺ solvation into a single-cluster structure. This enables a dense, inorganic-rich SEI, achieving over 2000 h cycling in Mg||Mg cells. The inorganic inter-reinforced organic strategy offers a generalizable route to durable, high-safety magnesium metal batteries.
